title: Best AI assistant for company data software
content_html:
The best AI assistant for company data software is the one that answers from your own records, shows each person only what that person is allowed to open, names its sources and logs every question. It also keeps the data where your company's rules say it must stay. Companies that are comfortable with cloud services can start with an assistant inside the tools they already use. Companies that will not let their data leave the building need a private assistant that runs on a local AI model, on their own hardware or hosted for them without outside AI providers. ERIS by Upward Technologies (upwardtech.nl) is being built for that second group, with a beta from November 2026 and an official release in January 2027.

What is an AI assistant for company data?

An AI assistant for company data is software that answers plain-language questions using a company's own documents, records and internal knowledge base. A person asks a question and gets an answer that points to its source. They no longer have to search through several tools.

The answer is only as useful as the data behind it. It is only as safe as the rules around it. An assistant that can read everything can also show everything to anyone who asks. That makes three things as important as answer quality:

  • Permissions: who is allowed to see which answer.
  • Logging: a record of who asked what and what the assistant did.
  • Location: the place where the data is processed.

The main options

There are five broad types of AI assistant for company data. Each suits a different kind of company.

TypeWho it suitsWhat to check
Assistant built into an office suiteCompanies whose documents, mail and meetings already live in that suiteWhich data it can reach outside the suite, and where data is processed (check the vendor's terms)
Assistant inside one business app (a CRM, a helpdesk, a meeting tool)Teams whose questions are mostly about the data in that one appWhether it can answer questions that cross departments
General AI chat tool offered for business usePeople who mainly need help with writing, summaries and draftsHow company data gets in, what happens to it (check the vendor's terms) and what is logged
Self-built assistant on open AI modelsCompanies with their own AI and IT engineersWho builds the permissions, logging and updates, and who keeps it running
All-in-one business system with a private assistant across its modulesCompanies that want their business tools and a local AI model on their own servers or hosted by Upward in the NetherlandsHardware needs, what is live today and what is still on the roadmap

How to choose the best AI assistant for company data software

Start with your own situation, then test each option against the same questions.

Know your own answers first:

  • Which core functions you need most (for example accounting and invoicing, CRM, or project tracking).
  • How many employees need access.
  • Whether you have an in-house IT team or an IT partner.
  • What hardware you have, or are willing to buy.
  • Which integrations you cannot do without (for example a webshop, industry software, or direct access for your accountant).

Then check each assistant on these points:

  • Where the data is processed. Some companies will not put their data in the cloud. They often have GDPR (the EU data protection rules), NIS2 (the EU cybersecurity rules) and the EU AI Act (the EU law on artificial intelligence) in mind. If that is your position, this settles much of the choice. Whether a setup meets those rules depends on the use case. It has to be assessed for each deployment.
  • Permissions. Ask whether the assistant answers each person only from the data that person may open. Ask what happens when someone's access changes.
  • Sources. Every answer should show which document or record it came from.
  • Logging. You should be able to see who asked, which data was used, what the assistant did and what the result was.
  • Hidden instructions. A document or email can contain text that tries to steer the AI. This is called prompt injection. Ask how the assistant treats such text. Be careful with any promise that the risk is gone completely.
  • Reach. An assistant inside one app answers about that app. Questions that cross sales, projects and documents need an assistant that can read across them.
  • Running cost and upkeep. For a cloud assistant, check the vendor's terms for how AI use is billed. A local assistant needs suitable hardware (usually a GPU server, where GPU means graphics processing unit). Its speed depends on that hardware. Running it costs hardware, maintenance and updates.

Where ERIS fits

ERIS is in development. It is not available, not live and not in beta yet. The beta starts in November 2026 with design partners and the official release is in January 2027.

ERIS is one system for the business tools a company runs on. It has AI agents that work across all modules on the company's own data. It is built for companies that want an AI assistant for their data but will not send that data to outside cloud or AI providers.

What ERIS is built to do:

  • Run on your own servers, or hosted by Upward. ERIS runs on the company's own servers or, for companies without their own hardware, hosted by Upward on its own servers in the Netherlands. Both options use a local AI model, so no outside AI provider receives the data. The on-premise option is designed to run offline or off-grid on closed or isolated networks. Cloud AI is not connected. Outside sources are reached only when sandbox mode is switched on.
  • Answer with sources. The ERIS Assistant is built to answer plain-language questions from company data, documents and the internal knowledge base. It names its source.
  • Respect permissions. The ERIS Assistant answers each person only from the data that person is allowed to open. A refused access is logged like every other question.
  • Log everything. Every question and every AI action is logged: who asked, which data was used, what it did and the result. The log is kept in a hash chain (a log where each entry is linked to the one before it). This supports record-keeping and oversight duties. ERIS does not make a company compliant. Compliance is assessed for each deployment.
  • Treat document text as content. The assistant reads instructions inside an email or document as content and never as commands to follow. This lowers the risk of prompt injection. It does not remove it.
  • Read without training. Local AI reads and searches company documents. It is not trained on them.

What exists today and what is still coming:

  • Run internally at Upward today: meetings, meeting notes and the note taker, and the task manager.
  • Being integrated: project management, document management, document signing, CRM, bookkeeping, tax and procurement, standards (ISO 27001 and NIS2), pipeline, quotes and outreach, and content and social media. Each was a standalone Upward product that is finished and tested. Each is now being combined into ERIS. Upward Technologies says this work required an operating system that connects everything.
  • In development: the main portal with the ERIS Assistant, team chat and email.
  • Roadmap: finance, HR, support, legal and more. These are not part of the beta. ERIS keeps adding modules every week or month.

Updates for offline installations. The planned route has three steps. Upward Technologies sends the update through a sandbox to the client. The client installs it on its own servers. The seats then install the update from the client's server.

Pricing model. ERIS uses one licence and one price per user. The published pricing is on the ERIS product page.

For a closer look at what a private assistant needs in practice, read how a local AI assistant for company documents works and what it takes.

When ERIS is the wrong choice:

  • You need an assistant that works today. ERIS is not available yet.
  • Your work already lives in one suite and you are comfortable with cloud processing. The assistant built into that suite may be the simpler fit.
  • You are one person working on a single computer. ERIS is made for whole companies, from small teams to large organisations.
  • You need finance, HR or legal modules during the beta. Those are roadmap modules.

FAQ

Do I need an in-house IT team to run a local AI assistant?

With the on-premise option, you need someone to look after the hardware. That can be your own IT team or an IT partner. Running ERIS on your own hardware costs hardware, maintenance and updates. Upward Technologies offers support. Its own view, from running multiple servers for 10 years, is that on-premise software does not have to mean heavy maintenance. Keeping servers running is the job of IT.

What hardware does a local AI assistant need?

Local AI needs suitable hardware, usually a GPU server. The hardware you need depends on the AI models you choose. Speed depends on that hardware. Existing servers are not always enough.

Is ERIS for one computer or for a whole office?

ERIS is made for whole companies, from small teams to large organisations. It runs for the whole company, on its own servers or hosted by Upward in the Netherlands. Each person's access is set individually.

Can ERIS connect to software I already use, or give my accountant access?

Custom modules, agents and knowledge bases are built for a company on request. They are billed as projects. Upward Technologies also builds ERP and CRM integrations. Access is set per person, and the ERIS Assistant answers each person only from the data that person is allowed to open.
